title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
why_read: A solid robotics paper on giving humanoid robots the ability to react to physical forces during manipulation tasks, relevant to those working in embodied AI.
analysis: FLORE teaches a humanoid robot to control not just where its hands move but how much force they apply, using demonstrations collected with force-sensing handheld grippers and body trackers. A diffusion-based policy predicts both motion and force targets, which a whole-body controller then executes while keeping the robot balanced. The reported jump from 26.7% to 80% success rate on contact-rich tasks compared to a position-only baseline is a meaningful improvement for a real engineering problem in humanoid robotics. This is of niche but genuine interest to robotics and controls engineers.
